RE: RFB C26-09 – Water Meter Installation Project

Dear Mr. Brassfield and the MSUA Board of Trustees:
Thirkettle Corporation, dba Utiliuse, is grateful for the opportunity to propose our water meter installation services
to the Miami Special Utility Authority (“MSUA”) in response to RFB C26-09, Water Meter Installation Project, due
July 7, 2026.
As MSUA advances its AMI initiative, the success of a 7,000-meter exchange depends not just on the meter, but on
the team in the field installing it. That team captures accurate data, handles each customer call and visit
professionally, and keeps the project on schedule. That is precisely what Utiliuse was built to do. As the installation
arm of Thirkettle Corporation, we install meters and endpoints and coordinate our work with the Authority's chosen
system.
Our experience with projects like this is current and close to home, built over the more than thirty years Thirkettle
Corporation has served the utility sector. Our field group has worked on over 200 AMR and AMI deployments, from
300 services to more than 280,000, and we have installed over one million meters, radios, and metering devices
nationwide. Most recently, we are completing a large project for the City of Norman, Oklahoma, covering roughly
43,000 installations. That project included full meter exchange, endpoint installation, customer notification, call-
center support, staging, logistics, and project management. At several times the size of this one, it puts a job of
exactly this kind squarely in our recent track record.
For MSUA, we will install your Neptune Mach 10 meters and cellular endpoints and capture the field data the scope
requires for each install. We deliver that data in a flat file that integrates with your Tyler Incode billing system. Every
site, work order, and photo runs through NovusCenter, our cloud-based work-order management software, so the
Authority can see progress and quality in real time. We are an employee-owned company, licensed to do business
in Oklahoma, and we are confident we can finish the full exchange inside your nine-month schedule.
We would welcome the chance to present our approach to the Board of Trustees in person. Thank you for your
time and consideration.

Company Overview
Thirkettle Corporation has spent more than thirty years in the utility metering industry, supplying and supporting
metering products, Automated Meter Reading (AMR) and Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) systems, and
conservation and resource management solutions for water, electric, and gas utilities. Our knowledge of metering
comes from the product side, where we have served as the authorized distributor for a leading metering
manufacturer across Texas, Louisiana, and California, and built a firsthand understanding of meters, endpoints, and
AMI systems. We created Utiliuse, our installation arm, to carry that expertise into the field nationwide, on projects
across manufacturers, including Neptune, and beyond our distribution territory. From that base, we have taken our
installation services across the country, into states including Arizona, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, and
Oklahoma.
In 2013, we became employee-owned through an Employee Stock Ownership Program (ESOP). Ownership grows
with time invested, so the person managing your project and the crew at the meter box have a direct, personal
stake in getting it right.
Field Installation Services
Providing installation services to our utility partners started as an idea, but quickly became reality with the creation
of Utiliuse. We began by managing meter installation and water conservation work across the southwestern United
States, offering meter testing, auditing, and right-sizing programs. Since then, we have grown into a full-service
utility partner that delivers comprehensive installation services nationwide.
We built that capability on Thirkettle Corporation’s product-side knowledge of meters and systems, which shapes
how we install them in the field. To date, we have installed over one million meters, radios, and advanced metering
and conservation devices across the southern, midwestern, and western United States, spanning more than 200
AMR and AMI deployments sized from 300 to over 280,000 meters. Across Thirkettle Corporation we are
performing meter exchange services for the City of Norman, OK; Amarillo, TX; and New Orleans, LA, among other
active projects.
Thirkettle Corporation’s Selma, TX facility handles inventory management, staging, and project logistics for
installations across our service territories, and we track every work order through NovusCenter, our proprietary
work-order management software built for meter installation projects.
We perform our installations through a combination of our own staff and a trusted, first-tier subcontractor. We
have not finalized subcontractor selection for this project, and we will base that choice on availability and fit at the
time of award. Any subcontractor we select will be a qualified, experienced installation firm, and we will stay directly
involved throughout, providing our own Installation Supervisors on site at all times.

Experience and Past Performance
Over the past decade, we have completed water meter and endpoint deployments for utilities of every size, from
a few thousand services to several hundred thousand. The four projects that follow are a representative sample,
chosen because they match this project in scope, scale, or setting. Each one called for the same core work MSUA
needs: a full meter exchange, endpoint installation, accurate field data capture, customer coordination, and
disciplined project management. Full contact information is provided within our complete Client Reference List
enclosed herein.
The following information is confidential.
City of Norman, Oklahoma, Approximately 43,000 services
The City of Norman, Oklahoma is our most recent and most relevant project for MSUA, and it is now in its final
phase of field production, with closeout expected no later than August 2026. We were awarded the contract in
April 2024 to exchange approximately 43,000 residential and commercial water meters, including a number of
retrofits. Ahead of each exchange we notified customers with mailed postcards, then followed up at completed
sites with door hangers, supported by a call center that handled customer questions and limited appointment
scheduling. To run the project, we handled on-site logistics with temporary storage containers, pallet jack and all-
terrain forklift rental, and dedicated waste and recycling bins.
Brien Kiser and Brad Foley led the work, and both are on the team we are proposing for MSUA. This makes Norman
more than a comparable reference. The crews, project managers, customer-notification approach, and logistics
behind it are proven, current, and ready to carry over to a 7,000-meter exchange in the same state. MSUA would
not be hiring us to learn this work. We are already performing it at roughly six times the scale, and we can bring the
same team and process to Miami inside the Authority's nine-month schedule.
Fort Worth Water Department, Texas, Approximately 280,000 Services
Fort Worth Water Department (FWWD) issued its RFQ in September 2015 and selected Thirkettle Corporation dba
Aqua-Metric as prime contractor, with the contract subsequently executed in October 2016. At the time it was one
of the largest AMI deployments in the state, covering roughly 230,000 services at the outset and growing past
280,000 as the system expanded. As a turn-key AMI system, the project included network buildout, meter and
endpoint installation, software integration, and the support that followed.
To support work at this scale, we leased and furnished a project warehouse and staffed it with a warehouse
manager, and at the utility's request we placed a dedicated full-time on-site project manager for the life of the
build. The project was funded through the Texas Water Development Board and carried DBE participation goals,
which we supported through outreach workshops with local chambers of commerce. The real test was volume: our
crews installed and brought online more than a quarter-million meters and endpoints on an expedited two-year
schedule, coordinating site access, scheduling, and customer notification across the entire service territory. The
project was successfully closed out in October 2022.
For MSUA, Fort Worth is the clearest measure of our capacity. A 7,000-meter exchange is a small fraction of what
we delivered there, and it would draw on the same systems, supervision, and project discipline that kept a quarter-
million-meter deployment on an expedited two-year schedule.
WaterOne, Kansas, Approximately 150,000 Services
WaterOne, in the Kansas City suburb of Lenexa, is one of the largest water utilities in the state, and we served as
the installation subcontractor to its AMI system provider. The work ran in two phases: pilot and full deployment.
The pilot covered a small portion of endpoint installations on the utility's existing meters, and full deployment
followed. Altogether, the project’s total was approximately 150,000 endpoint installations. For each phase we set
up on-site storage containers, a temporary recycling container, and hazardous waste disposal for the removed

Project Approach
Utiliuse brings together a team with years of experience deploying meters and metering components, and we
execute every installation with a consistent focus on safety, accuracy, and clean data. Our methods are built on
best practices drawn from more than twenty years of field service for utilities across the country, and our project
supervisors oversee the work from mobilization through closeout. For MSUA, that means a full exchange of roughly
7,000 water meters and the installation of their cellular endpoints, carried out alongside the Authority's team and
on the Authority's schedule.
The following information is confidential.
Description of Services
Installation Approach
We are proposing water meter installation services as described in this section. Our scope assumes that each
account's meter and endpoint are installed together in a single visit, along with the field survey the project requires,
so the exchange and all required site data are captured in one trip without returning to the site. Before any notice
to proceed, we will work with MSUA to build a complete project schedule.
Project Planning Phase
During planning, we work closely with MSUA to develop and refine the scope of work. We prefer to begin with a
short series of workshops, where we align on responsibilities, deliverables, product storage and facilities,
scheduling, blackout dates, production targets, and timelines. We also pull service-address data from the billing
system and import it into NovusCenter, our work-order management software, so every account is staged before
crews reach the field.
Project Preparation and Mobilization Phase
During preparation and mobilization, we set up our operations around the warehouse and staging space MSUA
provides and establish the process for checking product out from the Authority's warehouse. We procure the tools
and mobile devices our crews need for the meter exchange and endpoint installation, and we mobilize field crews
and any special equipment to the project area. Before any installations begin, every technician attends an
orientation covering project requirements, safety training, and how we communicate with customers.
Deployment Phase
Our field crews work under our deployment management and supervisor team to carry out the scope, and every
site is managed through NovusCenter. The field supervisor assigns work orders to installation personnel, and at
each account the technician captures the required data and notes: the final and initial reads, the old and new serial
numbers, identification of the service-line material on the customer and MSUA sides, before, during, and after
photographs, and the GPS location of the meter box. Where the endpoint requires it, we drill the meter box lid to
seat the antenna, priced per the lid-drilling items added in Addendum No. 1. When a site is non-standard or needs
work beyond the standard exchange, the technician notifies MSUA's designated inspector before proceeding and
flags the account in NovusCenter. If the inspector cannot be reached, the technician returns the site to its original
condition, records the issue and location, and moves on, coming back once MSUA provides direction.
Our data analyst monitors the quality of the data in NovusCenter, and our field supervisor performs weekly
inspections on a random sample of completed sites to verify workmanship and data accuracy. NovusCenter runs
automated checks throughout, and our office staff cross-check uploaded data against the technicians' records.
Project Closeout Phase
During closeout, we work with MSUA to resolve any outstanding field issues. Route verification against the
Authority's receiving equipment is coordinated with MSUA and its AMI vendor, who are responsible for read
verification and read success rates. Once everything is addressed to MSUA's satisfaction, we demobilize our crews
and equipment and return any remaining MSUA-owned product to the Authority's facility.

Qualifications & Certifications
Our installation technicians are trained in the deployment and troubleshooting of metering and AMI equipment. The
hands-on training each receives means most situations that arise in the field are handled promptly and correctly. Our
senior technicians hold the water licenses that keep them familiar with the function and structure of a utility distribution
system, and we will carry the state and local licensing required for this work in Oklahoma.
Safety carries equal weight on every project, for our technicians and for the public around them. Our field staff are trained
in proper safety procedures, including driver safety, first aid, and hazardous conditions, and our senior and commercial
technicians maintain OSHA confined space entry certifications. Our installation supervisor leads weekly safety reviews with
the crews throughout the project.
Staffing and Identification
We require all personnel to pass background checks and routine drug testing, and we can provide that documentation to
MSUA on request, separate from this response and within the limits of the law. Our field technicians stay easily identifiable
throughout the project: each works in uniform with a photo identification badge and a high-visibility safety vest, and every
vehicle is marked on both the driver and passenger sides with magnetic signs displaying the project logo.

NovusCenter™ Software
As a resource and installation management company, Thirkettle Corporation quickly realized the demand to
manage and track various facets throughout a project in one singular repository; however, the market is limited in
offering operations and processes management software. Thus, NovusCenter was created to deliver a robust and
scalable solution to bridge smart utility assets with their managing devices.
As an asset management and automation software, NovusCenter serves as a cloud-based integration portal and
repository which allows utility personnel to view their entire system from any device with internet access. Detailed
real time data is delivered to provide an unparalleled view of the distribution system while allowing increased levels
of control and management. NovusCenter will efficiently manage your most critical resources and assets.
NovusCenter is designed with light weight GIS and work-order management functionality to track and monitor
assets such as water meters, electric meters, endpoints, and any other utility asset. Various modules are available
to manage metrology equipment, meter installations and readings, leak/conservation product, distribution
automation, infrastructure automation, pressure controls, and environmental safety.
NovusCenter can give the Utility an opportunity to integrate data from multiple sources and view in a single system.
This data can include:
                                                                                      NovusCenter – Asset Management
  •     Detailed asset information.
  •     The ability to view utility assets on a map.                                    1.   Web-Based Software
                                                                                        2.   Custom Integrations
  •     The ability to add data to the device or asset, such as: pressure,              3.   Device and Meter Readings
        temperature, flow, etc.                                                         4.   Consumption Profiles
  •     Provides control through interface.                                             5.   Multi-Site Visibility
  •     The ability to chart information related to asset.                              6.   Multiple Users
  •     View asset history.                                                             7.   Dashboard to Show Status
                                                                                        8.   Integrated Mapping
NovusCenter has an inventory tracking and validation application giving the
Utility more tractability for the lifecycle of the asset, from the original order
to disposal.
Likewise, NovusCenter’s mobile application, Serveiz is a wireless field application which allows direct contact with
utility staff. This allows utility personnel the ability to send and receive paperless work orders in real time, resulting
in carbon footprint reduction, and improved response time to critical issues. The mobile application is key to
increasing operational success as a field data collection solution with the use of mobile devices to capture work
orders and related information while in the field. The mobile system can support real time updates via cell network,
if needed, or periodically synchronize with local database storage when the mobile device is connected via Wi-Fi.
Serveiz can also capture new informational data through its survey tool functionality. This software can capture
important asset information and manage its use using work order processes. Data capture can be achieved via voice
to text, barcode scanning, or direct data entry.
The Serveiz application can simplify your entire service operation by using mobile applications that enable field
service technicians to work with or without network connectivity. By automating workflow, field service
representatives can efficiently receive, complete, and document assignments, manage equipment assets, and
capture expenses and critical site data for operations analysis and reporting. NovusCenter delivers automated
capabilities intended to streamline and improve management of field service activities and helps deliver
information to field technicians when they need it most.
Work Order Processing
NovusCenter runs on a mobile application for Android and iOS phones and tablets, so technicians work from cloud-
based software in the field rather than standard handheld equipment. Each device carries everything needed to

barcode scanner. NovusCenter also supports talk-to-text to speed data entry. We provide every installation
technician with their own device, and we extend NovusCenter access to MSUA personnel on their own devices as

After award, we work with MSUA to integrate NovusCenter with the Tyler Incode billing system. We can define the

Each day, technicians download their assigned work orders. We ask that work orders be released in daily or weekly

possible. As an added check, our office staff cross-check every uploaded record against the technician's field
documentation, a quality audit that covers one hundred percent of our installations.
At the end of each day, technicians confirm with our technical support staff that every installation has uploaded
successfully. We transfer swap files to MSUA at agreed intervals, typically weekly or at the completion of each route,
to push field data into the Tyler Incode billing system. Our technology team works with MSUA throughout to confirm
the data lands correctly and meets the Authority's standards.

Use of Subcontractors
The RFB requires all subcontractors performing more than 10% of the Work to be listed in the bid response, along
with documentation supporting their ability to complete the required Work. At the time of this submission, Utiliuse
has not finalized subcontractor selection for this project. Utiliuse respectfully requests the ability to provide
complete subcontractor information and qualification documentation prior to contract execution, following award.
Utiliuse represents that any subcontractor selected will be a qualified, experienced installation firm, and that
Utiliuse will provide its own supervisors on-site at all times.
Project Schedule
Our plan is to complete the full meter exchange within MSUA's nine-month schedule, and we have built our
approach to protect that date. We anticipate a Notice to Proceed roughly 30 to 45 days after the bid opening, and
the nine-month clock begins there. Once we receive the NTP, we move immediately into project planning,
integrating NovusCenter with the Tyler Incode billing system, importing route data, and preparing the customer-
notification campaign. Mobilization follows close behind: we organize our inventory and checkout process at the
warehouse MSUA provides, orient our crews, and run a first route to confirm our process before scaling to full
production.
Deployment is the heart of the schedule, and we run it route by route in the cycle order MSUA provides. We staff
the project to hold a production pace that completes roughly 7,000 meters inside the nine-month window, for all
standard work. We track production daily in NovusCenter and report progress to MSUA on a recurring basis, so the
Authority can see at any point whether we are on pace.
In the final month, as deployment concludes, we verify completed routes against MSUA's receiving equipment,
resolve any open items, and close the project out. This nine-month schedule reflects the standard scope of work.
Non-standard conditions and other delays beyond our reasonable control are addressed in our Exceptions and may
extend the timeline accordingly.

Pricing Clarifications and Assumption
We thank the Miami Special Utility Authority once again for the opportunity to present our meter installation
services. We believe our proposal meets the requirements set out in the bid documents, and we offer the following
clarifications so the Authority fully understands the basis of our response.
The following information is confidential.
1. Standard Terms and Conditions
Utiliuse has prepared this proposal using the information MSUA furnished in the RFB for their Water Meter
Installation Project. Our response is not intended as acceptance or rejection of any specific term or condition except
where expressly stated, and we reserve the right to negotiate a mutually agreeable contract with the Authority.
Where we propose changes to the Authority's bid documents, those redlines are included in the Exceptions portion
of this section for the Authority's review and discussion.
We also propose that the project's formal Scope of Work be developed jointly with MSUA after award, rather than
submitted with this bid. A scope drafted together ensures both parties share the same understanding of
responsibilities and deliverables before work begins, and it keeps our proprietary scope language out of the public
record. We are prepared to move quickly on both the redlined documents and the joint Scope of Work so that
contracting stays on schedule.
In recognition of fluctuations in material and labor costs, our pricing will be held firm for 180 days from the bid due
date, after which it may be subject to adjustment based on prevailing market conditions and supply chain factors.
Utiliuse has reviewed the specifications provided by MSUA to prepare our response in accordance with the project
scope as presented. Our team has inspected a small portion of accounts in effort to identify common site conditions
or potentially unique situations. While we believe our proposal to be a comprehensive solution for the Authority’s
consideration, we remain mindful that potential unknown conditions may not have been identified or disclosed
prior to our response which may arise through the course of the project. In such event, we will work closely with
the Authority on a case-by-case basis to determine how we best approach any unforeseen circumstances equitably
for both the Authority and Utiliuse.
Subcontractors: To facilitate MSUA’s Water Meter Installation Project, Utiliuse will endeavor to provide the best
field services team available. Our field meter exchange and endpoint installation will be performed by a qualified
installation subcontractor, under the direct supervision of our own personnel. If awarded, we intend to engage in
an individual subcontract with the selected subcontractor for their respective services of the project. Pricing as
provided is based upon our general understanding of the plans and specifications of the Authority’s RFB and may
be subject to additional cost(s) in the event of scope refinement or change. Supplemental third-party suppliers
included within our response may be contingent on Utiliuse’s award, potential scope changes, and/or final mutual
agreement(s) between Utiliuse and its third-party suppliers.
2. Proposal Pricing Clarifications
Utiliuse’s cost proposal is not all-inclusive. It is quoted based on our understanding of the services we are to perform
and the materials MSUA provides, as described in this response. Alongside MSUA's Bid Sheet, we have included our
itemized quote, which provides a complete breakdown of the products and services in our bid, including costs that
may not be part of the scope, such as installation incidentals. MSUA's Bid Sheet provides line items for the removal
and installation of meters only. To quote the project accurately, we also have to account for other services, including
field deployment management, mobilization, our work-order management software, and bonding. To complete the
Bid Sheet, we calculated an average cost for these services and folded it into our per-meter installation pricing. If
awarded, we will invoice each individual line item as shown in our itemized quote, rather than combined as on the
Bid Sheet. Because the folded per-meter allocation is rounded to the nearest cent, the Bid Sheet's unit prices,
extended totals, and grand total may differ from our itemized quote by a small amount. The itemized quote reflects

the precise pricing and governs actual invoicing, and the two reconcile to within rounding differences. Any service
not specifically itemized in our quote will incur additional fees and will require MSUA's approval and a change order
before the work is performed.
Inclusions – Each standard meter exchange unit price covers the field work to complete the exchange at a standard
site: vacuum-truck cleaning of the box or pit, identification of the line material on both the customer and MSUA
sides, reuse or replacement of the existing bushing adapters (labor only), and meter tail replacement (labor only).
For meters three inches and larger, the unit price also includes confined space entry, dewatering, and scheduling.
Several supporting services are folded into the unit prices on the Bid Sheet but listed separately on our itemized
quote, and we invoice them as separate line items. These include mobilization, NovusCenter work-order fees, and
the advance notification postcard and post-installation door hanger.
Non-Standard Installations – Where an installation is found to be non-standard as defined in the RFB, such as non-
working curb stops, broken or leaking pipes, collapsed meter boxes, or restricted access, we notify MSUA's
designated inspector before performing additional work. Authorized non-standard work is quoted separately based
on the conditions at the service site and must be approved before we proceed. Excessive downtime while our crew
awaits MSUA's inspector is billed at the hourly rate submitted on the Bid Sheet.
Bid Quantities and Contingency – The bid forms in the RFB and Addendum No. 1 do not list quantities. We have
filled in the quantities we can support from the meter counts provided in the addendum, including the meter
installation, lid modification, and salvage line items. For the remaining line items, including the hourly wage rate for
non-standard work, meter box tile replacement, setter replacement, and curb stop replacement, we are unable to
account for the quantities in advance, so we have entered a quantity of one on the bid form as a placeholder. That
number is not an estimate of the actual need. Since those quantities are unknown, we recommend that MSUA
budget a 25% contingency (i.e., $515,000.00) to cover these and other incidental items. We have not included this
contingency in our cost proposal, but we strongly recommend it.
Lid Drilling Quantities – Our pricing for drilling holes in existing meter box lids is based on estimated quantities of
75% metal lids and 25% plastic lids. This split reflects a brief site visit we conducted ourselves and is not a full audit
of MSUA's system. The quantities are estimates and are subject to change based on the lids actually found in the
field.
Billing System Integration – Our pricing includes the cost of integrating NovusCenter with MSUA's Tyler Incode
billing system. The billing platform may impose separate fees for data extract and meter-swap integration with
NovusCenter. We cannot determine those fees, as they are arranged directly between the billing-software provider
and MSUA, and we understand from the RFB that MSUA is responsible for the costs of the interface into utility
billing. We assume the billing-software provider will impose a one-time integration charge, though in some cases
the required work can increase the utility's annual fees. We are not responsible for any new or revised fees imposed
by third-party software providers. Any integration between field data and the Neptune 360 or Landis & Gyr MDMS
is coordinated by MSUA with those vendors.
Performance, Payment, and Maintenance Bonds – Bond pricing is included in our response. It is based on an
estimated 12-months from the date of contract execution. Bond costs are subject to change at one percent of the
premium for each additional month beyond the estimated duration and on the total contract value at project
completion.
TAXES AND FEES. All prices quoted are exclusive of federal taxes, state taxes, municipal taxes, tariffs, duties, and
other government-imposed fees (collectively the “Taxes and Fees”) related to the procurement, installation, and
delivery of materials and equipment. Customer shall be liable for all applicable Taxes and Fees imposed upon the
Goods purchased. Taxes and Fees will be added to each applicable invoice and are the responsibility of the
Customer. If Customer is exempt from sales tax, Customer is required to provide all applicable tax exemption
documentation at the time of purchase. Any changes in Taxes and Fees may result in adjustments to the final invoice
accordingly.

3. Installation Assumptions
Utiliuse defines a standard meter exchange service as a like-for-like meter replacement with no lay-length variance,
and with all information provided by the Utility regarding meter type and accessibility. Utiliuse assumes all metering
data as it pertains to characteristics (size, model, etc.) or any special requirements will be furnished by the Utility
in advance of the meter exchange services with minimal exceptions. If the installation technician is unable to
complete a standard meter exchange service due to inaccurate characteristics, the account will be Returned to
Utility (RTU). Additional trip charges may apply for inaccuracies in data, issues outside our control causing extended
delays in service timeframe, or multiple visits to a single service account site to complete the meter exchange
service.
An installation scope of work will be provided during contract execution based on Utiliuse’s understanding of a
standard meter installation service. Should the Utility request to modify the scope of work to include more custom
services, pricing is subject to revision.
All materials for the standard exchange are furnished by MSUA. Any part not provided by MSUA may be supplied
at cost plus fifteen percent.
Pricing is based on meter boxes set in dirt.
For boxes or sets in concrete or asphalt, our pricing covers the meter exchange only. It does not include box
adjustments, curb stop replacements, or other modifications at those locations. We can modify plastic or metal
lids, but not concrete lids. Any modification at a concrete or asphalt site requires a site inspection, for which a fee
applies, followed by a separate quote based on that inspection.
Our base pricing includes vacuuming each meter box or pit with a meter vac truck. We assume each box is
vacuumed before work begins and remains clear until the exchange is performed. MSUA will provide water for the
vac truck, typically from a hydrant, and a location to dispose of spoils.
Pricing assumes MSUA will provide all storage requirements that Utiliuse personnel can access throughout the
Project. This includes, and is not limited to, the following: product storage/warehousing and material handling;
temporary use of specialty equipment as needed (i.e., forklift, pallet jack, etc. for unloading of delivered material –
if we are required to perform this service); parking spaces for field technicians during loading / unloading of
material; site to dispose of dirt, trash, cardboard, and/or spoils; office space for field management personnel, as
needed; and access to wireless internet connection.
Hazardous Waste Removal Fee – It is our understanding that MSUA does not have any existing endpoints and all
existing meters are mechanical. However, if it is found that any removed legacy product requires hazardous waste
removal, additional fees will apply. This will be invoiced at cost plus 15% to the Utility.
Pricing assumes the following end-customer notification initiative will be adequate for MSUA’s meter exchange
project: one (1) Notification Postcard to be delivered to each service address at least one week prior to the meter
exchange, one (1) post-installation door hanger left upon completion of the exchange, or if we are unable to
perform the service. Because we make up to three attempts at each account, pricing budgets up to three door
hangers per account. Should the Utility require an alternate notification campaign, this can be provided at a
different cost.
All meters removed from service are returned to the facility MSUA designates.

Any account which the meter is unable to be located, is inaccessible, requires special equipment, additional
materials, or labor to successfully complete will be flagged as Returned to Utility (RTU). No additional work will be
provided without prior authorization from the Utility.
In the event an account is flagged as RTU, Utiliuse will transfer all responsibility to the Utility and be relieved of any
responsibility of returning to the account in effort to complete a meter exchange. Service accounts flagged as an
RTU will be returned to the Utility for further action and Utiliuse may, in its sole discretion, invoice the Utility for
the trip charge for the initial site visit, and for each additional site visit thereafter.
 •    The Utility may request Utiliuse return to an RTU account to perform the meter exchange service, at which
      time Utiliuse may invoice for the meter exchange. In the event a technician returns to an RTU account not
      inside the active route being work at the time of the technicians return and is unable to perform the services
      during the additional attempt resulting in an additional RTU, Utiliuse may invoice the Utility for a Site Visit fee
      for the trip.
 •    Our price proposal reflects an inserted line item for a possible RTU Fees. This will be applied for the time
      needed to collect data at the service point. Furthermore, the Utility will have full access to this data within
      NovusCenter along with pictures.
Standard Water Meter Installation Services are non-inclusive of the item(s) detailed in our Non- Standard
Installation Services and/or any special plumbing requirements on either the distribution or consumer side. Non-
Standard Installation Services will be priced with the assumption the service work will be performed during the
initial site visit. The Utility may preauthorize any or all of the Non- Standard Installation Services in advance to
prevent delays in production schedules. Non-Standard Installation Service pricing may increase if the services are
requested after the initial site visit.

Exceptions Listing
Utiliuse has reviewed the RFB for MSUA’s Water Meter Installation Project in full, and we are excited to present
our installation services to the Authority. A project of this scope deserves careful diligence, and our intent
throughout has been to prepare a response that positions both parties for a successful partnership.
In the ordinary course, we would prefer to work through contract terms collaboratively with the Authority, outside
a bid response, and reach a shared understanding before anything is finalized. We understand the Authority instead
asks bidders to identify proposed changes now, within the response, and to execute the contract within ten days
of acceptance. Since that window leaves little room to resolve open terms after award, and because the bid security
is tied to it, we have set out our proposed modifications here so that nothing is left to interpretation later.
Utiliuse can generally comply with most of the conditions in the bid documents, including much of the EJCDC
Standard General Conditions of the Construction Contract. As the Authority noted in Addendum No. 1, several of
those provisions are written for new construction and do not apply to an owner-supplied meter-installation service.
We agree, and our redlines make clear which provisions we read that way, so that what is "applicable" is understood
the same way by both parties rather than left open under a ten-day execution deadline.
With that in mind, we reserve the right to negotiate a mutually agreeable contract with the Authority. Our response
is based on the information available in the bid documents, and we expect some refinement through discovery and
negotiation. We ask that any such refinement be treated not as a material default, but as the normal work of
aligning scope ahead of a successful implementation.
The clarifications and deviations below set out the items we want to be sure the Authority sees clearly. As noted in
our Clarifications section above, we also propose developing the project's formal Scope of Work jointly with the
Authority after award, which is the cleanest way to settle scope and expectations on both sides. A redlined copy of
the solicitation follows at the end of this section showing our proposed modifications. If our scope of services
changes through that process or through negotiation, pricing may be adjusted to reflect the services ultimately
agreed upon.
We understand these proposed changes factor into your evaluation, and hope they read as what they are: a good-
faith effort to contract responsibly and to deliver a meter installation program the Authority can rely on.
The following information is confidential.
1. Additional Clarifications and Deviations
This bid is expressly conditioned on the Authority's acceptance of the exceptions stated herein. If any material
exception is not accepted, no contract is formed and Utiliuse may withdraw its bid without forfeiture of bid security.
Meter Boxes and Sets in Concrete or Asphalt. Our pricing is based on meter boxes set in dirt. At locations where the
box or setter is in concrete or asphalt, we will perform the meter exchange but take exception to box adjustments,
curb stop replacements, or other modifications at those sites. We cannot modify concrete lids, which are prone to
cracking, though we can modify plastic or metal lids. Any modification at a concrete or asphalt location requires a
site inspection, for which a fee applies, followed by a separate quote based on that inspection.
Site Restoration. We take exception to restoring surrounding surfaces, particularly concrete and asphalt, to their
original condition. Because we vacuum each box before the exchange, soil disturbance is minimal, and we level any
minor excess soil into the surrounding area. Where an exchange would significantly disturb surrounding
improvements such as landscaping or shrubbery, we place the site on hold and coordinate with the Authority before
proceeding. We repair and restore only within the limits of our installation warranty, consistent with Addendum
items 32 and 51.
Maintenance Bond. The RFB requires a maintenance bond equal to the contract price covering defective
workmanship for two years after acceptance. We propose a twelve-month maintenance bond instead, limited to

16914 Alamo Parkway, Bldg. 2, Selma, TX 78154

defects in our workmanship and excluding owner-furnished materials, manufacturer defects, pre-existing
conditions, and third-party damage. This change is reflected in our redlined agreement, and we flag it here as an
item we would like to settle in negotiation.
Installation Warranty. In place of the warranty provisions in the bid documents, our redlines substitute our standard
installation warranty. In summary, we warrant that our services are performed in a professional and workmanlike
manner; we warrant the meter installation against defects in our workmanship for thirty days from the date the
work is performed; we pass through the manufacturer's and supplier's warranties on the owner-furnished meters
and endpoints; and we exclude implied warranties, consequential damages, and defects caused by abuse, third-
party work, normal wear, or pre-existing conditions. The full language appears in the redlined agreement.
Standby and Project Suspension. If the project is suspended through no fault of ours while our crews are deployed,
we reserve the right to invoice a daily rate per on-site employee to offset idled labor, and we may demobilize until
the suspension is lifted. We recognize the Authority's position that standby time is not separately compensated,
and we offer this as a point for discussion.
Force Majeure and Owner-Caused Delays. We propose that delays beyond our reasonable control are not treated
as a default and do not trigger liquidated damages, and that the contract time be extended accordingly. These
include late delivery or shortage of the meters and endpoints MSUA furnishes, delays caused by MSUA or its other
contractors, and delays in inspector availability or site access. The Force Majeure clause was not modified in our
redlines, so we raise it here for the Authority's consideration.
Mobilization. MSUA's Bid Sheet does not include a separate line item for mobilization, and the addendum states
there are no separate mobilization costs. To complete the Bid Sheet, we fold our mobilization cost into the per-
meter installation price. On our itemized quote, mobilization is broken out as its own line item, and if awarded we
intend to invoice it on that basis.
Liquidated Damages. Utiliuse acknowledges the liquidated damages provision in the Contract Agreement, set at
$200 per working day in Addendum No. 1. While we can accept liquidated damages for delays within our reasonable
control, we cannot accept liability for delays caused by MSUA, by the delivery lead times of MSUA-furnished meters
and endpoints, by third parties, or by the events described in Force Majeure and Owner-Caused Delays above. We
ask that the Contract Agreement clearly define the conditions under which liquidated damages apply. All meters
and endpoints MSUA furnishes must be on site before the project start date, and we cannot be held responsible
for delays caused by the unavailability of MSUA-furnished materials. Our timeline is based on the work proposed in
this response, so additional or excessive work beyond that scope, and weather delays as described below, must
extend the contract time without exposure to liquidated damages.
Weather Delays (Addendum item 76). We take exception to absorbing weather delays within a fixed schedule. We
cannot account for unforeseen weather delays, particularly catastrophic weather that constitutes a force majeure
event, and the contract time must be extended for weather delays of any kind.
Pricing Is Not All-Inclusive (RFB p.3, Examination of Bid Documents; p.15, care and protection of the work area). We
take exception to the requirements that our bid include all costs necessary to complete the work, and that all care
and protection of the work area be treated as incidental and included in the unit price. Our pricing is not all-
inclusive. Some requirements are taken as exceptions and others are not quoted, as described throughout this
section.
Subsurface and Unforeseen Conditions (RFB p.3). We take exception to investigating subsurface conditions and
preparing our bid accordingly. Assessing subsurface conditions system-wide would require a full site survey, which
is not part of a bid response, so we cannot guarantee against unknown conditions. Our technicians are responsible
only for conditions visible at the time of work and cannot account for underlying or unforeseen conditions that are
not observable.

Pre-Existing Conditions and Water Quality (Addendum item 58). We take exception to responsibility for complaints
arising from known or pre-existing conditions, including water quality issues such as rust or sediment stirred up by
re-pressurizing the line. These are not caused by our work, and MSUA would field those customer calls.
Workmanship Inspection (RFB p.15). We accept MSUA's right to inspect and approve workmanship before
acceptance. That approval does not extend or alter our installation warranty, which remains thirty days, nor does
it extend of alter our monthly billing period.
Survey Scope (Addendum item 62). Service-line material identification is performed within the meter box only and
is limited to what is visible. We take exception to excavating outside the meter box for this purpose.
Receiving Equipment (Addendum item 26). The RFB references the Zebra MC3300 with Itron software for route
verification. Since MSUA is deploying Neptune meters on a Neptune system, Itron software does not align with the
equipment being installed.
Read Verification and Read Rates. Our responsibility is to install and activate each meter and endpoint correctly.
We are not responsible for read verification or read success rates. Confirming that endpoints communicate to the
AMI network, and the ongoing read performance of that network, is the responsibility of MSUA and its AMI vendor.
Setter Stabilization (Addendum item 48). We take exception to including stabilizing material or a stabilized setter in
our standard pricing, as the number of sites requiring it is unknown and cannot be quoted across the project. We
request the ability to discuss and negotiate this during contracting.
Special Job Hours. If a water line springs in after meter removal, if new meters do not fit standard gaskets, or if a
setting requires a complete replumb, special job hours or appropriate fees apply. We take exception to absorbing
this work in the standard exchange price, as these conditions are unpredictable and cannot be quoted across the
project.
Insurance Requirements (RFB p.4). Our current coverage differs from the RFB's insurance requirements in several
respects. Our commercial general liability policy carries a $1,000,000 per-occurrence limit and a $4,000,000
aggregate, rather than the $5,000,000 aggregate required. We also carry a $10,000,000 umbrella, but it is excess
coverage, and we understand the RFB requires these limits to be met by the underlying policy itself rather than by
reference to umbrella or excess coverage. Our workers' compensation policy carries a $2,000,000 limit, below the
$5,000,000 aggregate the RFB specifies. We do not currently carry a separate Contractor's Pollution Liability policy.
Our policies also provide thirty days' notice of cancellation for reasons other than nonpayment, which differs from
the ten-day notice the RFB requires. We believe we can meet these requirements if required, though the additional
coverage would carry additional cost, and we did not have the information from the Authority or the time needed
to obtain a quote before the bid deadline. We therefore present these as exceptions and would welcome the
opportunity to finalize acceptable coverage with the Authority.
End confidential information.

                                        EN

performing water meter installations and replacements for the Miami Special Utility Authority. The
purpose of this document is to ensure consistent, high-quality installation practices, accurate data

installation firm to complete the Work.

  Standard Installation:
  The following description is the standard installation for the utility.
      •    Installation is for meters in sizes 5/8x3/4 up to 8”.

      •    All meters are equipped with a working curb stop or shut off valve.

      •    Residential meters sizes 1” and below are in an accessible water meter box.

      •    Commercial meters up to size 8” are in an accessible water meter box or meter
           vaults.

      •    Meters are installed with meter couplings on both sides of the meter allowing for




                                                                      AL
           easy removal and installation of the new meter.

      •    There is adequate room within the meter box for a contractor to easily work
           around and remove meter.




                                                            TI
      •    Meter boxes may be filled with dirt which must be removed by contractor in order
           to access and identify material type on customer and MSUA side and the
                                            EN
           necessary components.

Water Meter Exchange:
  For standard installations as described above, it shall be the responsibility of the Contractor to
  complete the following Work.
                        D
      •    Safely remove meter box cover and verify meter number.

      •    Attempt to notify customers if they are home. If there is no answer, check to see
                     FI

           if meter is turning. If turning, come back later or wait a few moments to see if
           meter stops turning.
                    N



      •    Take photos before, and after installation of the water meter.

      •    Turn curb stop off.
          O




      •    Identify and record material type on customer and MSUA side
 C




      •    Record final reading from old meter.

      •    Remove old meter.

      •    Install new meter and washers.

      •    Open customer spigot(s) to flush air and debris from house line.

      •    Slowly turn curb stop on.

      •    Verify the new meter is turning.

   customers’ consumption automatically metered, and is now taking the next steps to implement
   the new network.

Miami Special Utility Authority (MSUA) Regular Meeting
MEETING DATE:         August 18, 2026

AGENDA TITLE:         Discussion and Possible Vote to Award Request for Quote (RFQ) 26-62 Lease Purchase
                      Contract for One (1) 2027 AM55E Bucket Truck From Altec Industries, Inc.

PRESENTER:            Derric Lollar

BACKGROUND:
We requested 36 month interest rate quotes from 4 area lending institutions for the lease purchase of a 2027
AM55 Bucket Truck. The Sourcewell price and the amount to be financed is $337,245.00.
